posts.title: The family (couch lineup)
posts.igCaption:
Today's couch lineup — a few of the builds so far. 🪵

Demolition timber, construction timber from a building site, the shelves of a garden house, an old beech staircase handrail — every one of these was something else before it became a guitar. Wood that already lived a life, now on its second one.

Sixto Rupes · Sixto Tignum · Sixto Loculus · Sixto Gradus

The next one's already on the bench. Follow along.

Website: link in bio or scan the QR at the end.

#handmadeguitar #luthier #reclaimedwood #customguitar #sixtocustomguitars #oneofone #guitarbuilder #belgianmade #woodwithastory
posts.igCaptionLong:
Lined a few of them up on the couch. Not all of them made it to the photoshoot: one is out being tested, others are prototypes that never leave the workshop. My couch has never looked this good.

None of this wood came out of a timber catalogue. Demolition timber: Sixto Rupes. Construction timber from a building site, which turned Sixto Tignum into a featherweight. The shelves of the garden house that became my workshop: now the top of Sixto Loculus, my first real semi-hollow. Part of an old beech staircase handrail, now living on as a bass: Sixto Gradus. Wood that already lived a life — and now gets a second one, with strings on.

Every build is a one-of-one: designed around one idea, never repeated. And yes, there's already a new body glued up in the workshop. You'll see it come together here.

posts.ytTitle: Guitars that were something else first | Sixto Custom Guitars
posts.ytDescription:
A few of the builds so far, lined up on the couch: Sixto Rupes, Sixto Tignum, Sixto Loculus and Sixto Gradus. Demolition timber, construction timber from a building site, the shelves of a garden house, an old beech staircase handrail: every one of these was something else before it became a guitar.

Every Sixto is a one-of-one, handmade in Belgium from reclaimed wood, each with its own Latin name. The next one is already on the bench.

posts.title: Two guitars, one garden house (Casula + Loculus)
posts.igCaption:
My house came with a garden house. It became my workshop.

The wood of its shelves became the top of Sixto Loculus. The wood I still had left from it became the herringbone top of Sixto Casula.

Two guitars. One garden house. Loculus: Latin for a small compartment. Casula: a little house.

What would you build from the place you live in?

posts.title: Ebony, 12" radius (Horreum)
posts.igCaption:
An ebony fretboard for Horreum. 🪵

Rough-cut to a 12" radius with my router and radius jig. That curve is what your fingers feel on every chord. Next up: sawing the fret slots. Only then does it get sanded true.

Ever wondered why some necks just feel right? Ask me anything below.
